dataflow.outcome: persistent local denial of service for task-reading commands until task state is repaired
dataflow.sink: runtime memory/CPU consumed by unbounded line/descriptor allocation and map retention
dataflow.source: pre-adoption control of task JSONL line size, strings, collection cardinalities, record count, and task IDs
dataflow.summary: adopted `.kcs/tasks.jsonl` -> `BufRead::lines()` -> `serde_json::from_str()` -> late path/hash checks -> `BTreeMap` retention -> status/batch consumers

impact.why: One adopted scope can repeatedly wedge local task-reading commands through memory and CPU exhaustion.

likelihood.why: Exploitation requires copied/preseeded task-state adoption and a sufficiently large valid payload.

reachability.attacker: lower-trust contributor to copied or preseeded task state
reachability.outcome: status, index, and recovery workflows repeatedly allocate on oversized state
reachability.summary: The attacker needs pre-adoption control of supplied KCS task state and the victim must run a task-reading command. The vector is local to one adopted scope and has no network listener.

attackPath.summary: A lower-trust contributor supplies an adopted or preseeded KCS scope with a huge valid `tasks.jsonl` record or many unique records. When the operator invokes status, index, or batch recovery, KCS allocates and retains attacker-shaped task state before rejecting poisoned fields.

codeEvidence.code:
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct TaskDescriptor {
    pub task_id: String,
    #[serde(rename = "type")]
    pub task_type: TaskType,
    pub mode: Option<MarkdownizeMode>,
    pub input_path: String,
    pub input_hash: String,
    pub previous_raw_hash: Option<String>,
    pub parent_run_id: Option<String>,
    pub changed_unit_keys: Vec<String>,
    pub output_ref: String,
    pub unit_keys: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub status: TaskStatus,
    pub attempts: u32,
    pub next_retry_at: Option<String>,
    pub deadline: Option<String>,
    pub heartbeat_at: Option<String>,
    pub fallback_reason: Option<String>,
    pub created_at: String,
codeEvidence.explanation: Adopted task state controls `task_id`, `input_path`, strings, `changed_unit_keys`, and `unit_keys`; the default serde shape has no field-level size or cardinality cap.
codeEvidence.label: Task descriptor carries unbounded strings and arrays

codeEvidence.explanation: `BufRead::lines()` grows the complete line and `serde_json::from_str()` materializes the complete descriptor before KCS applies task-specific controls.
codeEvidence.label: Reader allocates a full line and descriptor before validation

codeEvidence.explanation: The path and hash checks reject poisoned semantics only after deserialization. Valid records with unique `task_id` values are retained in the `BTreeMap`, so cumulative record count also consumes memory.
codeEvidence.label: Semantic controls and map retention happen after allocation

codeEvidence.explanation: Routine status output invokes `TaskStore::all()`, so an oversized adopted `tasks.jsonl` blocks normal inspection and recovery workflows.
codeEvidence.label: Status command reads all task state

codeEvidence.explanation: The existing loop is the natural place to add total-file, per-line, record-count, string-length, and vector-cardinality limits before descriptor allocation and retention.
codeEvidence.label: Reader should bound bytes and cardinality before retaining tasks

regressionTests: Reject over-limit lines before JSON deserialization.
Reject task files exceeding the record-count budget.
Keep path/hash validation after bounded parsing.
Ensure `kcs status` surfaces bounded corruption without unbounded allocation.
remediation.summary: Enforce total task-file size, per-line byte length, record count, string length, and vector cardinality before deserializing or retaining task descriptors. Return a bounded corruption/recovery error when limits are exceeded.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that adopted task state must be bounded before KCS materializes records. The reader accepts a complete task JSONL line, deserializes all strings and collections, and retains unique descriptors before any size, cardinality, or record-count control exists.

summary: `TaskStore::all()` reads adopted `.kcs/tasks.jsonl` records into an unbounded line string and deserializes all task strings and key arrays before enforcing path and hash controls. A lower-trust preseeded scope can therefore wedge status, index, or batch recovery through memory and CPU consumption before the poisoned state is rejected.
title: Oversized task JSONL records allocate before validation

assertions: Per-line allocation is not bounded before `String` growth.
Serde collection allocation is not cardinality-bounded before semantic checks.
Unique task IDs are retained in a `BTreeMap` until the full result vector is returned.
limitations: No OOM-sized payload was generated; practical RSS thresholds were not measured.
validation.method: saved target-runtime bounded controls plus local synthetic PoC
validation.summary: Saved validation parsed one 38,318-byte record with 512 `changed_unit_keys` and 512 `unit_keys`, retained 64 unique records, and showed a poisoned path is rejected only after the same arrays are parsed. The included PoC reproduces that ordering with synthetic local records.
